chunks: Assembly-line tests and their steps. The question: What sort of tests do PCBs undergo on the assembly line? What are the steps?
After a board leaves the soldering oven, it goes through tests in a set order: cheap and safe first, powered and expensive last. First it is inspected.
Then an unpowered electrical test checks for shorts and wrong parts. Next it is powered with a current limit, loaded with firmware, and given a functional test.
Failures go to repair and are retested.
Think of checking a new house before moving in. You walk through to see that everything is built, then test the wiring for faults with the power off.
Only then do you flip the main switch, and perhaps through a safety breaker. After that you try the lights and appliances.
Turning power on first risks a fire from a fault you could have found in advance. A board is the same, and the current limit plays the breaker.
The ordered flow with the repair loop. Dashed arrows are failures routed to repair; after repair the board restarts the test sequence.
Unpowered test: electrical checks done without power, so a fault cannot damage anything. Current limit: a supply setting that caps current so a fault cannot burn parts.
Programming: loading firmware (the program stored in the board's chip) and the serial number into the board.
Functional test: powering the board and checking it behaves like the product. Repair loop: failed boards are diagnosed, fixed and retested.
A 3. 3 volts board draws about 85 milliamps when idle. You set the supply's current limit to 150 milliamps, enough to start up but low enough to protect the board.
After power-up you measure the idle current. A reading between about 60 milliamps and 120 milliamps passes, and anything outside fails.
If it passes, you load the firmware and run the functional test. That is the whole idea.
"After reflow I'd expect AOI, and X-ray for BGAs, then an unpowered electrical test, in-circuit or flying probe, for shorts, opens and component values.
Then a current-limited first power-up, programming the firmware and calibration, and a functional test of rails, clocks, interfaces, sensors and outputs.
Mains products get a safety test like hipot, some get burn-in, and then final inspection and packing.
The order is cheap and safe first, expensive and powered last, with failures going to repair and retest."
Quick check. Why is the unpowered electrical test done before the first power-up?
